amendments.done_when: A merge to main runs only the Linux groups and cancels the main run it supersedes; macOS and Windows run nightly, on release tags and on demand; and the test timing file covers today's suite so each platform's groups take about the same time

done_when: A merge to main runs only the Linux groups and cancels the main run it supersedes; macOS and Windows run nightly, on release tags and on demand, and those full runs never reuse a Linux-only parent's results; and the test timing file is refreshed to cover today's suite

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Raise: Functional. The normal release procedure now stalls before tagging. docs/guide.md:319–321 tells maintainers to confirm that the merge commit’s `forge-next` run on main passed the full Linux, Mac and Windows matrix. This changed matrix gives main pushes only the Linux groups, so that required result cannot exist. The guide needs to direct maintainers to a full run that this workflow actually starts.
findings.title: Release instructions require a full main run that no longer exists

why: Main's full run takes 20 to 35 minutes on every merge and fills the shared runners that pull requests wait for: all three platforms run on each merge, superseded runs are not cancelled, and the test timing file is a week old so groups are uneven
